title: How a string in a file becomes a typed field
summary: The Binder walks your target type, asks each property source for a name it might have under any relaxed spelling, converts what comes back, and assembles the object.
entry: Put a breakpoint in Binder.bindObject and start an app with any @ConfigurationProperties class. It recurses, so the first few frames show the shape of the whole algorithm.

steps.notice: The public entry point. Everything below is one recursive descent from here, so read this signature and then follow bindObject rather than trying to read the class top to bottom.
The three-way branch that is the whole algorithm: is this an aggregate (list, map, array), a plain property, or a data object whose members need binding one at a time? Everything else is detail.

Where relaxed binding actually happens. The Binder asks each source for one canonical name; matching the many spellings is the source's job, not the Binder's. That division is why an environment variable binds and the same spelling in a properties file does not.
Chooses between constructor binding and setter binding by asking the BindConstructorProvider. This is the line that decides a record just works while a mutable class needs setters.
Every value arrives as a String and leaves as the declared type. Note that the target is a ResolvableType, not a Class, which is how List<Duration> converts element by element.
